attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack post, closing a passage he wrote himself.

semantics.note: The 'maybe' hedge is about Nadella's private confidence, and the proposition leaves that open. 'Certainly not taking any chances' is firm wording, and reading it as hedging against reliance on OpenAI is faithful to the context (Mistral, an internal big model).

contract.note: The plain reading (keeping active alternatives to OpenAI, not getting rid of every risk) is the ordinary, informed reading. Continued cooperation with OpenAI is correctly treated as not contradicting it.

evidence.note: Microsoft CTO post, dated May 6 2024 via e2. Confirms in-house model building, naming MAI. This is a company disclosure, but it describes observable activity.
Dated May 6 2024 report: Microsoft is building MAI-1 (~500B parameters) under Suleyman, aimed at competing with OpenAI and others.
The quoted line shows Copilot still runs on GPT-4. That limits the claim to diversification, not independence. The same article also reports MAI-1 development.

reviews.rationale: As of May 6 2024, dated reporting and Microsoft's CTO confirm active internal development of large models (MAI-1), giving Microsoft options beyond OpenAI. Microsoft's continued reliance on GPT-4 does not meet the contradiction condition. Microsoft was keeping alternatives, as Marcus said.

attribution.note: Marcus's own assertion in his own post.

semantics.note: 'But they are' firmly asserts present direct competition. The rescue is a background premise, fairly rendered as the employment offer.

contract.note: Reading direct competition as selling overlapping products to the same customers is the ordinary meaning. Using April 2024 as the period, the latest reported before publication, is reasonable.

evidence.note: Reuters, April 2024: Altman pitched ChatGPT Enterprise to executives who were already Microsoft customers. That is overlapping enterprise offerings sold to the same buyers.
Bloomberg, Dec 2023: Microsoft said it would hire Altman after his dismissal. This establishes the 'rescue' premise that the support condition requires.
OpenAI's Aug 2023 announcement shows the enterprise product existed before the target period. It is background only.

reviews.rationale: Reporting from April 2024 shows OpenAI pitching ChatGPT Enterprise to Microsoft's existing enterprise customers, who asked why they should pay twice. That is direct commercial competition. Bloomberg confirms Microsoft's offer to hire Altman after his firing. Both parts of the support condition are met, and nothing in the packet contradicts them.
